name: Decode-phase GEMM: memory-bandwidth bound at batch size 1
arithmetic_intensity: At batch size 1, the GEMM is memory-bandwidth bound: each weight is loaded from HBM and used for only one multiply-accumulate. The arithmetic intensity is ~1 flop/byte, far below the GPU's ridge point.
workarounds: Weight-only quantization (INT4, FP4) reduces bytes per weight, directly improving memory-bound throughput
Batching increases arithmetic intensity but reduces throughput for interactive workloads
Speculative decoding increases effective batch size for the target model
MoE routing reduces active parameters per token
notes: This is the fundamental reason why weight-only quantization (W4A16) works: at decode time with batch size 1, the GEMM is memory-bound, so reducing weight bytes directly increases tokens/s. The Marlin kernel achieves near-ideal 4x speedup because it reduces weight bytes by 4x (from FP16 to INT4). This is also why the SGLang kernel selection issue is so impactful: when NVFP4 is served with Marlin (W4A16) on pre-Blackwell hardware, the weight bytes are reduced but the activation bytes are not, so the speedup is less than the theoretical maximum. The decode GEMM is the dominant cost at batch size 1, which is the common case for interactive inference.
